newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota yet to agree on Indian car venture.
newsitem.headline: Toyota yet to agree on Indian car venture.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said on Wednesday it is still in negotiations with the Kirloskar group over a possible car joint venture in India.

The Yomiuri Shimbun, a Japanese daily, reported on Wednesday that Toyota had broadly agreed with the Kirloskar group to start producing vehicles in 1999 through the joint venture, and that Toyota planned to acquire 70 to 80 percent of the joint venture.
But a Toyota spokesman said talks were continuing.
"We are still in talks with Kirloskar and have not applied yet to the Indian government to set up the venture," a Toyota spokesman said.

In early June, the Press Trust of India reported that Toyota would invest nearly $240 million of a total of $340 million in the joint venture, which would start producing 1,500 cc diesel-engined 10-seater Kijang sports utility vehicles in 1999. It also said that Toyota would hold 70 percent of the venture.
Toyota declined to comment on that report.

In late May, Toyota executive vice-president Akira Yokoi told Reuters in Tokyo that the firm hoped to announce the joint venture agreement before the start of the company's summer holidays in Japan on August 9. Yokoi said Bangalore was one of four possible sites for the venture.

Japan's Suzuki Motor Corp currently has a market share of more than 70 percent in India's passenger car market, through a joint venture with the Indian government. Many carmakers have entered the Indian market aiming to wrench market share from Suzuki, industry sources said.
